note: Fixed RQ2 question set (docs/rq2-protocol.md). The same ten questions for every repository; Q9 and Q10 cannot be answered from the mined data and measure appropriate refusal. 'expected' tells annotators what a covering answer must contain.

standard.text: What are the main parts (folders or modules) of {repo} in the latest mined snapshot?
standard.expected: Names at least three top-level folders or modules that appear in the latest snapshot's structure.

standard.text: Which mined commits changed the dependencies between files the most? Name the commits.
standard.expected: Names at least one commit (hash) with the largest number of dependencies added or removed, with the numbers.

standard.text: When was the most recent architectural change in the mined history, and what did it change?
standard.expected: Gives the commit (hash) and date of the newest change with architectural changes, and what it added or removed.

standard.text: Which files were involved in the most recent recorded change evidence?
standard.expected: Lists source files of the newest change evidence, or says none is recorded.

standard.text: How has the number of files changed across the mined snapshots?
standard.expected: Compares the file count of an older and a newer snapshot (with hashes or versions) and says whether it grew or shrank.

standard.text: Who authored the commits that changed the architecture?
standard.expected: Names the author(s) of at least one commit with architectural changes, with the commit.

standard.text: Did any mined commit remove dependencies between files? Which one, and how many?
standard.expected: Names a commit with dependencies removed and the number, or correctly says none did.

standard.text: What is the oldest snapshot shown in the project data, and what did the project look like then?
standard.expected: Gives the oldest listed snapshot (hash, date or version) and its file count.

standard.text: Why did the maintainers of {repo} choose this architecture instead of a different one?
standard.expected: Declines or says the data does not record the reasons; any stated reason is unsupported.

standard.text: How many people use {repo} in production today?
standard.expected: Declines or says the data does not say.
